Great question! The good news is you don't need much to get started. Here's what helps when tasting:
What you'll need:
✓ A glass — Any small glass works, but a Glencairn glass (tulip-shaped) is ideal because it amplifies the aromas and lets you properly smell the spirit. You don't need to pour more than three-quarters of an ounce.
✓ Water — Have plenty on hand to alternate sips and clear your palate. Adding a bit of water to your whiskey can also "open up" the spirit and reveal finer notes. Use spring water or soft tap water (skip the ice for tasting).
✓ Simple snacks — Unflavored, unsalted crackers or small slices of bread help cleanse your palate between samples, especially with bold flavors.
What comes in the Tasting Box:
The box itself includes the 3 vials (45ml each) and tasting notes to guide you — so you're basically ready to go once it arrives!

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Great question! Here's exactly how to taste whiskey properly for the first time:
Step 1: Set Up
Pour a small amount (about 3/4 ounce) into your glass
Have water and crackers nearby
Skip the ice — it dulls the flavors
Step 2: Smell First (The Aroma)
Gently bring the glass up to your nose — don't rush! You don't want to overwhelm your senses. Some people even sniff with one nostril first, then both. Take your nose away after each sniff and trust the first thing you smell. Repeat and other layers will reveal themselves. Can you identify familiar smells? (The tasting notes in your box will help!)
Step 3: Taste (The Palate)
Take a small sip and roll the spirit over your tongue and around its sides, then throughout your mouth. Savor the flavors and start identifying them — are they woody? Fruity? Spicy? Herbal? Notice the texture and intensity too.
Step 4: Add Water (Optional)
After your first taste, add a bit of water to the glass. This "opens up" the spirit and lets your nose and mouth detect finer notes by taking the edge off the alcohol.
Step 5: Cleanse & Repeat
Alternate sips of water and whiskey to clear your palate. Use crackers between samples. Give your nose breaks with fresh air when needed.
Pro tip: The Tasting Box includes tasting notes to guide you through what to look for in each whiskey — follow along and you'll learn as you go!
